name: merge
description: Combine several JSON documents into one. Use at a join, where two branches have each produced a result and the step after them needs both: named puts each under its own name, shallow and deep merge their fields. Each document is a part_<name> parameter. Every part must be a JSON document, so a step that answers in prose is not one of them.

strategy.description: named keeps each part whole under its own name, and is the one to use at a join. shallow merges the parts into one object, a later part replacing a field an earlier one set. deep does the same but merges a field that is itself an object rather than replacing it.

^part_[A-Za-z0-9_]+$.description: One document to combine, named by what follows part_. Write one of these per document: part_review: "{{ steps.review.text }}" and part_tests: "{{ steps.tests.text }}" produce {"review": …, "tests": …}. The order they are written in is the order they merge in.

output_schema.description: One JSON document, pretty-printed. Under named it is an object with one key per part, holding whatever that part was, including a scalar. Under shallow and deep it is the parts merged, so every part has to be an object.

exit_codes.2: invalid input (stdin was not a JSON object, no part_<name> was given, a part is not a string, or strategy is not one of the three)
exit_codes.5: malformed data (a part is not JSON, or is the result of a step that did not run)
exit_codes.6: refused (shallow or deep was asked for and a part is not an object)
